questions.q: According to this lesson, what turns a vendor's SIG response like "we encrypt data at rest" from a mere statement into an enforceable obligation?
options: Nothing — questionnaire answers are always legally binding on their own
The contract specifying that the vendor must meet that standard and stating what happens if it doesn't
The vendor's marketing website repeating the same claim
A verbal confirmation from the vendor's sales representative
questions.explain: An assessment answer is just a statement of fact until the contract requires it, specifies the standard, and defines consequences for non-compliance — that's the gap between assessing a vendor and governing one.

questions.q: Why do real vendor contracts specify a concrete breach notification window, such as 24 to 72 hours, instead of language like "notify us promptly"?
options: Because "promptly" is functionally unenforceable, and the customer's own regulatory notification clock (such as GDPR's 72 hours) is already running
Because longer notification windows are always illegal under every regulation
Because vendors are required by law to notify customers only once per year
Because "promptly" was banned as a contract term by the Cloud Security Alliance
questions.explain: "Notify us promptly" has no enforceable meaning. A concrete window lets the customer actually meet its own regulatory deadlines, which start running regardless of when the vendor gets around to notifying it.

questions.q: In practice, how is a right-to-audit clause most often satisfied against a large cloud or multi-tenant provider, according to this lesson?
options: By sending a team of auditors to physically inspect every data center the vendor operates, every year
The clause is never included in cloud vendor contracts at all
By the vendor providing its SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certificate, and completed questionnaire annually, with literal audit rights reserved for Tier 1 relationships or triggered after an incident
By the vendor refunding the full contract value if it refuses an audit request
questions.explain: Large providers can't allow literal on-site audits for every customer with an audit clause. In practice, annual evidence (SOC 2, ISO 27001, questionnaire) satisfies the clause day to day, with literal audit rights held in reserve.

questions.q: What does a subcontractor flow-down requirement in a security addendum accomplish?
options: It automatically terminates the contract if the vendor ever uses any subcontractor
It transfers the customer's regulatory accountability to the subcontractor
It only applies to subcontractors located outside the vendor's home country
It requires the vendor to impose equivalent security obligations on its own subcontractors and notify the customer before adding a new one with data access
questions.explain: Flow-down addresses fourth-party risk directly — it makes the vendor extend equivalent security obligations down to its own subcontractors and requires disclosure before a new one gets access to customer data.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say contractual depth (full security addendum, audit rights, breach notification timelines) should scale with vendor tier rather than apply uniformly to every vendor?
options: Because low-tier vendors are legally exempt from having any contract at all
Because negotiating that depth takes real legal and procurement effort, which should be concentrated on vendors that actually hold sensitive data or system access
Because only government vendors are allowed to sign security addenda
Because contractual depth has no relationship to the risk tiering covered in the previous lesson
questions.explain: Full security addenda take real negotiating effort on both sides. Applying that same depth to every vendor, including low-risk ones, wastes legal and procurement time that should go to the vendors that actually warrant it.
